title: Merge a parcel into the gap in a running belt's line, square and clear of its neighbours, before the scanner
instruction: Put the parcel from the side table onto the running belt, into the empty gap in the line of parcels, square to the belt, so that it has at least 4 cm of clear belt on both sides when it reaches the scanner arch. Let go of it before it reaches the scanner. Don't touch the other parcels. The belt keeps running.
context: Parcel sorters are fed at induction and merge stations, where parcels from a side table are put onto a running line into the empty slots between parcels already on it; the barcode scanner and sorter downstream need each parcel square and clear of its neighbours, and the line does not stop. Done by: induction workers and induction robots in parcel hubs and distribution centres. The parcels are small: 9 x 6 x 5 cm, the size of small boxed items such as pharmacy or cosmetics cartons on the induction belt of a small-item sorter in e-commerce or pharmacy order fulfilment, whose belts are narrow to match.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table (1.10 x 1.30 m) whose edges are 65 cm either side of the midpoint between the bases. A straight belt conveyor crosses the table parallel to the line through the bases, its centre line 32 cm in front of them, running from the robot's right to its left at 6 cm/s. Its grey steel bed (18 cm wide, 1.5 cm thick) runs from 62 cm right to 110 cm left of the midpoint; past the table's left edge it stands on a dark steel post to the floor (6 x 4 cm, centred 105 cm left of the midpoint). On the bed lies a dark rubber belt (16 cm wide, 1 cm thick, 2 mm above the bed, so its top is 2.7 cm above the table) over the same length. A grey steel end stop (18 cm wide, 1 cm thick, rising 6 cm above the belt) closes the belt's left end. Four brown corrugated-cardboard parcels (closed boxes, 9 cm long along the belt, 6 cm across it, 5 cm tall, 150 g each) lie on the belt's centre line, square to it, in a line: from the right, the last parcel's trailing face 58 cm right of the midpoint, 6 cm of empty belt, the third parcel, an empty gap of 24 cm, the second parcel, 6 cm, and the front parcel, whose leading face is 14 cm left of the midpoint. A grey steel side table (a block 12 cm front to back, 16 cm along the belt, 2.7 cm tall, its top level with the belt's) stands between the belt and the left arm, centred 15.5 cm in front of the bases and 5 cm left of the midpoint, its far edge 1.5 cm from the conveyor bed; a fifth, identical parcel stands in its middle, square to the belt. A scanner arch stands over the belt 52 cm left of the midpoint: two dark steel posts (2 x 2 cm) on the table, their inner faces 9.5 cm either side of the belt's centre line, carry a dark steel head (23 cm across the belt, 3 cm along it, 3 cm thick) whose underside is 13 cm above the belt; a red line (4 mm wide) across the head's underside, 52 cm left of the midpoint, marks the scan line. The belt starts with the trial, reaching 6 cm/s in 0.5 s, and does not stop.
scoring: Each parcel passes the scanner from the moment its leading face reaches the scan line until its trailing face has left it. The clear belt between two parcels is the distance from the scan line to the next parcel's leading face at the moment the one ahead leaves the line (a photo at that moment). 0 if either arm or the merged parcel touches any of the four parcels of the line at any time in the trial (comes within 5 mm of it: pushing a neighbour to widen the gap, brushing one, bumping one while setting down; only two parcels that have both passed the scanner may touch, as they gather at the end stop); 0 if an arm touches the merged parcel (within 5 mm) at any moment of its pass under the scanner: it must be let go before it gets there, not held on the belt or steered through; 0 if the line arrives at the scanner disturbed (a backstop for a touch between control steps): its spacing at the scan line more than 1.5 cm off how it started (6 cm between the first two and between the last two, 24 cm from the second to the third), one of the four more than 1.5 cm across the belt from its centre line as it reaches the line, or turned or tilted more than 5 degrees during its pass; 0 if any parcel, at any time during its pass, is not lying on the belt (its underside more than 1 cm above or below the belt's top: lifted, carried, on another parcel, fallen off) or reaches over the belt's edge; if any of the five has not passed by the end of the trial; or if the side-table parcel did not pass in the gap, right after the second parcel and right before the third. Otherwise a third for each of: (1) 4 cm or more of clear belt between the second parcel and it; (2) 4 cm or more between it and the third parcel; (3) it passes square: turned 15 degrees or less from square to the belt and tilted 15 degrees or less from lying on its 9 x 6 cm face, throughout its pass. 1.0 when all three hold (the trial then ends with success 1 s after the last parcel has passed). Only a parcel's first pass counts.
reset_notes: Stop the belt, put the four parcels back in their line on the belt (the last one's trailing face 58 cm right of the midpoint, 6, 24 and 6 cm of empty belt between them) and the fifth on the side table, and start the belt with the trial. Parcels that passed the scanner are waiting against the end stop. On a real table the belt runs at 6 cm/s with side guards along its bed, a guard covers the pinch point between the queued parcels and the end stop, and an emergency stop within the operator's reach cuts both the belt and the arms; parcels are light (150 g) and the end stop keeps them from running off the belt's end.
fidelity: The belt is a long plate that stays in place while its surface moves: each physics step it gets a surface velocity and is put back, so parcels ride on it by friction, wherever set down. They ride about 1.1 cm/s slower than that surface (measured), so it is driven at 7.1 cm/s for a 6 cm/s line, slower than a real parcel line. The arms can't slow or stop it. Parcels are rigid boxes, friction 1.2/1.0. The scanner isn't simulated: clearances and orientation come from the parcels' poses.
